Challenge in this appeal is the order that is passed by the Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in M.V.C. No.7857/2019 dated 18.05.2022.

sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the insurance company which is arrayed as respondent No.2 in the Motor Vehicles case.

3. The two grounds urged by learned counsel Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, disputing the quantum of amount that is awarded as compensation are that the tribunal erred in deducting 1/4th of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased Rathan Kumar @ Kumar and NC:
2024:KHC:32574 indeed 1/3rd of the actual earning are required to be deducted.
4.

The second ground urged is that the deceased Rathan Kumar was aged about 48 years by the date of accident and therefore the appropriate multiplier that is applicable is '13' as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma and others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and another case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 but the tribunal erred in adopting '14' as multiplier.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The case of the respondent Nos.1 to 4 i.e., claimants is that the 1st respondent and 4th respondent are the wives of the deceased Rathan Kumar and respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the sons of late Rathan Kumar born through the 1st respondent.
Learned counsel Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, submits that there is no proof that the 4th respondent-Smt.Bharathamma is the wife of the deceased Rathan Kumar.

Learned counsel states that the dependents will be only respondent Nos.1 to 3 and NC:
2024:KHC:32574 therefore the tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3rd of the actual earnings of the deceased Rathan Kumar.

6. On the otherhand, the submission that is made by Smt.Sushmitha.G, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 4 is that the respondent Nos.1 to 4 produced sufficient proof with regard to their relationship with the deceased Rathan Kumar.

Learned counsel contends that the tribunal basing on the evidence produced, came to a conclusion that the respondent Nos.1 and 4 are the wives and respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Rathan Kumar.
7. A perusal of record reveals that respondent Nos.1 to 4 produced Aadhaar cards and ration card which are marked as Ex.P-9 to Ex.P-14 to show their relationship with the deceased Rathan Kumar.

The tribunal at para 15 of the impugned order highlighted the cross examination of PW-1 where it was suggested that for the past 14 years the deceased Rathan Kumar was residing with respondent No.4 i.e., his second wife only.

Thus, the testimony of NC: 2024:KHC:32574 PW-1 and the documentary evidence produced establishes the relationship of the 4th respondent with the deceased Rathan kumar and that the respondent Nos.1 and 4 are the wives of the deceased Rathan Kumar and respondent Nos.2 and 3 are his children.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the plea taken in respect of deduction of amount towards personal and living expenses of the deceased Rathan kumar needs no consideration.
8. The second ground as earlier indicated is with regard to the multiplier applicable.
It is not in dispute that the deceased Rathan kumar was aged around 48 years by the date of accident.

Therefore, as rightly contended by Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, learned counsel for the appellant, the appropriate multiplier to be applied as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma's case stated supra is '13' thus the tribunal has erroneously applied '14' as multiplier.

sentences.text: Also as rightly contended by Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, learned counsel for the appellant, the tribunal instead of NC: 2024:KHC:32574 awarding Rs.15,000/- as compensation under the head loss of estate awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.

Likewise, the tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.40,000/-
towards loss of spousal consortium and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.

However,
the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
Therefore, the award of the tribunal in respect of grant of compensation requires modification.

So for as loss of dependency is concerned, if calculated by applying the aforementioned parameters will be as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Notional income per month 14,000-00 Future Prospects 17,500-00 (14,000 x 25%)
Annual Income 2,10,000-00 (17,500 x 12)
Deduct 1/4th towards living 1,57,500-00 and personal expenses  Apply appropriate multiplier 20,47,500-00  '13'
 Loss of dependency 20,47,500-00  NC: 2024:KHC:32574 10.

Together with the aforementioned amount, the respondent No.1 to 4 are entitled to Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate and 15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
11.
The respondent Nos.1 and 4 are entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and likewise respondent Nos.2 and 3 are entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.

Thus, the total compensation which the respondent Nos.1 to 4 are entitled to is as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of dependency 20,47,500-00 Loss of Funeral expenses 15,000-00 Loss of Estate 15,000-00 Loss of Spousal consortium 40,000-00 Loss of Parental consortium 40,000-00  Total 21,57,500-00
Thus in the light of the foregoing discussion, the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is Allowed in Part.
